issues.description: The default base image string 'python:3.12' is duplicated across four locations, complecting one fact with four places.
issues.detail: A single value about the world (the default image) now lives in pipeline.py, the Jinja template fallback, Commands.ts catch-fallback, and CellMetadataEditor.tsx as DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE. The whole point of the RPC was to make one source of truth; instead you added three more. Pick one: server is authoritative, client renders what it gets, template trusts its inputs.

issues.description: A synchronous RPC round-trip to fetch a constant string is incidental complexity dressed as a feature.
issues.detail: get_default_base_image is a function that returns a literal. It introduces network failure modes, async state, a try/catch with a hardcoded fallback, and an extra state field, all to communicate one immutable value. Bake it into the labextension build, or include it in an existing config payload. The RPC is easy to add and not simple.

issues.description: Behavior change: empty base_image now silently becomes python:3.12 instead of deferring to KFP's default.
issues.detail: The comment above the changed line explicitly said 'Use kfp default image' by setting base_image to ''. Replacing that with DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE complects 'UI default for display' with 'compile-time default for execution' --- two different concerns at two different times. Users who relied on KFP's default get a surprise pin to 3.12.

issues.description: Replacing a visible Input with a modal hidden behind an 'IMAGE' button is easy to code, not simple to use.
issues.detail: The previous UI exposed the value as data on the surface. The new UI hides it behind a click, gates it on stepName being non-empty (an unrelated coupling), and adds dialog open/close state to the component. The user has to open a modal to see what image will run. That is more code and less affordance.

issues.description: defaultBaseImage is threaded through three component layers as a prop instead of read from context.
issues.detail: LeftPanel fetches it, passes to InlineCellsMetadata, which passes to both InlineMetadata and CellMetadataEditor. This is prop-drilling a constant. Either put it on CellMetadataContext (which already exists for this kind of cross-cutting metadata) or import it as a module constant once the duplication above is resolved.

issues.description: isDefault is derived from absence of baseImage, conflating 'unset' with 'matches default'.
issues.detail: createBaseImageText labels the row '(default)' whenever this.props.baseImage is falsy, even if pipelineBaseImage is set and overriding. The label is reporting on identity (was a value provided?) while the displayed string is a value (effective image). Those are two different facts; the UI should say which one it means.

review.summary: This PR takes one fact --- "the default base image is python:3.12" --- and scatters it across a Python module constant, a Jinja fallback literal, a TypeScript catch-block literal, and an exported TS constant, then wires an RPC to ferry it between them. That is the textbook shape of incidental complexity: a value problem solved with plumbing. Worse, the compiler-side change silently converts empty base_image from "let KFP decide" to "pin to 3.12," complecting display defaults with execution defaults at two different times. The UI change trades a visible Input for a modal behind a button gated on an unrelated field, which is easy to implement and not simple to use. Pick one source of truth, pass it as data, and put the default back on the surface.
